value.zh: 年十二，客有候其兄者，不过翻，翻追与书曰：“仆闻虎魄不取腐芥，磁石不受曲针，过而不存，不亦宜乎！”
value.en: When he was twelve, a visitor called on his brother but snubbed Yu Fan; Fan sent a letter after him: "They say amber ignores rotten mustard and a lodestone spurns a crooked needle—a slight delivered and unnoticed sits ill with neither party."
value.literal: At age twelve a guest came to call on his elder brother but passed by without stopping for Fan; Fan pursued him with a letter saying: "I have heard that amber does not pick up rotten mustard and the lodestone does not take a bent needle; to pass by and pay no heed—is that not fitting!"

value.zh: 客得书奇之，由是见称。〉
value.en: The guest read the note with admiration, and Fan's reputation began from that hour.〉
value.literal: When the guest received the letter he marveled at it, and from this Fan was praised.〉

value.zh: 太守王朗命為功曹。
value.en: The Administrator Wang Lang named him Clerk of Merit.
value.literal: Administrator Wang Lang appointed him Clerk of Merit.

value.zh: 孫策征會稽，翻時遭父喪，衰絰詣府門，朗欲就之，翻乃脫衰入見，勸朗避策。
value.en: While Sun Ce was marching on Kuaiji, Yu Fan was in mourning for his father; he appeared at the yamen gate in sackcloth. Wang Lang meant to comfort him, but Fan stripped the mourning garb, went inside, and urged Lang to withdraw rather than face Ce.
value.literal: Sun Ce campaigned against Kuaiji; Fan was then mourning his father and came to the administrator's gate in mourning dress with hemp cord. Lang wished to approach him, but Fan removed his mourning garments and entered to see him, urging Lang to avoid Ce.

value.zh: 朗不能用。
value.en: Lang would not follow his counsel.
value.literal: Lang could not employ him.

value.zh: 拒戰敗績，亡走浮海。
value.en: He fought and was routed, then fled by ship onto the open sea.
value.literal: He resisted in battle and suffered defeat, then fled and went out to sea.

value.zh: 翻追隨營護，到東部候官，候官長閉城不受，翻往說之，然後見納。
value.en: Fan stayed with the column as escort until they reached Houguan in the eastern circuit; the county magistrate barred the gates until Fan talked him round and won them entry.
value.literal: Fan followed to guard the camp; they reached Houguan in the eastern division. The chief of Houguan closed the city and would not receive them; Fan went and persuaded him, and only then were they admitted.

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：翻始欲送朗到广陵，朗惑王方平记，言“疾来邀我，南岳相求”，故遂南行。
value.en: 〈The Book of Wu adds that Fan first meant to see Wang Lang safely to Guangling, "but Lang trusted an inscription attributed to Wang Fangping—Hasten and summon me; the Southern Peak calls—and turned his course southward instead."
value.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Fan had first wished to escort Lang to Guangling; Lang was misled by Wang Fangping's inscription, which said Come swiftly and invite me; the Southern Marchmount seeks me, "and therefore went south."

value.zh: 既至候官，又欲投交州，翻谏朗曰：“此妄书耳，交州无南岳，安所投乎？”
value.en: At Houguan he planned to bolt for Jiaozhou; Fan warned him: "That text is nonsense—there is no Southern Marchmount in Jiaozhou; what harbor could such a sign point to?"
value.literal: After reaching Houguan he wished again to flee to Jiaozhou. Fan remonstrated with Lang: "This is a false inscription; Jiaozhou has no Southern Marchmount—where would you go?"

value.zh: 乃止。〉
value.en: Lang gave up the idea.
value.literal: Thereupon he stopped.

value.zh: 朗謂翻曰："卿有老母，可以還矣。"
value.en: Lang told him: "You have an old mother at home—you should go back."
value.literal: Lang said to Fan: "You have an aged mother; you may return."

value.zh: 〈翻别传曰：朗使翻见豫章太守华歆，图起义兵。
value.en: 〈Yu Fan's separate biography says Wang Lang dispatched him to Yuzhang's Hua Xin to plan raising loyal troops.
value.literal: 〈The Separate Biography of Fan states: Lang sent Fan to see Administrator Hua Xin of Yuzhang, plotting to raise troops in righteous revolt.

value.zh: 翻未至豫章，闻孙策向会稽，翻乃还。
value.en: Before he reached Yuzhang he learned Sun Ce was bearing down on Kuaiji and wheeled about.
value.literal: Before Fan reached Yuzhang he heard that Sun Ce was heading for Kuaiji, and Fan then returned.

value.zh: 会遭父丧，以臣使有节，不敢过家，星行追朗至候官。
value.en: His father had just died, yet as an accredited envoy he would not detour home; he marched nights until he caught Wang Lang at Houguan.
value.literal: It happened that he was in mourning for his father; as an envoy under orders he dared not pass his home, but traveled by night and overtook Lang at Houguan.

value.zh: 朗遣翻还，然后奔丧。
value.en: Lang released him to return, and only then could Fan observe the funeral rites.
value.literal: Lang sent Fan back, and only then did Fan go to mourn.

value.zh: 而传云孙策之来，翻衰绖诣府门，劝朗避策，则为大异。〉
value.en: The main narrative, however, claims that when Ce approached, Fan appeared at the yamen in mourning bands urging Lang to yield—quite another story.〉
value.literal: Yet the biography says that when Ce came, Fan in mourning dress went to the gate and urged Lang to avoid Ce—this is a great discrepancy.〉

value.zh: 翻既歸，策覆命為功曹，待以交友之禮。
value.en: Once Fan was back, Sun Ce restored him as Clerk of Merit and courted him as an equal.
value.literal: After Fan returned, Ce again appointed him Clerk of Merit and treated him with the courtesy due a friend.

value.zh: 身詣翻第。
value.en: He called at Fan's house himself.
value.literal: He went in person to Fan's residence.

value.zh: 〈江表传曰：策书谓翻曰：“今日之事，当与卿共之，勿谓孙策作郡吏相待也。”〉
value.en: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan records Ce's letter: "What we face now we shoulder together—do not imagine I would handle you like any county clerk."〉
value.literal: 〈The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ce wrote to Fan: "Today's affair I must share with you; do not think Sun Ce means to treat you as a mere clerk of the commandery."〉

value.zh: 初，山陰丁覽，太末徐陵，或在縣吏之中，或眾所未識，翻一見之，便與友善，終鹹顯名。
value.en: Ding Lan of Shanyin and Xu Ling of Taimo—petty clerks or men the world had never heard of—won Yu Fan's friendship at a glance and rose to renown.
value.literal: At first Ding Lan of Shanyin and Xu Ling of Taimo—some among county clerks, some unknown to the multitude—when Fan saw them once he befriended them, and in the end all became famous.

value.zh: 〈《会稽典录》曰：◎览字孝连，八岁而孤，家又单微，清身立行，用意不苟，推财从弟，以义让称。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu notes Ding Lan, styled Xiaolian: orphaned at eight from a poor house, he kept scrupulous conduct, gave his inheritance to a cousin, and earned fame for yielding.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: ◎ Lan, courtesy name Xiaolian, at eight sui was orphaned; his family was moreover humble; he purified himself and established conduct, his intentions never careless; he pushed wealth to a younger cousin and was praised for righteous yielding.

value.zh: 仕郡至功曹，守始平长。
value.en: He rose to Clerk of Merit and acting magistrate of Shiping.
value.literal: He served the commandery up to Clerk of Merit and acted as magistrate of Shiping.

value.zh: 为人精微絜净，门无杂宾。
value.en: Refined, punctilious, and austere, he admitted no casual callers.
value.literal: As a man he was refined, subtle, and cleanly austere; no miscellaneous guests crossed his gate.

value.zh: 孙权深贵待之，未及擢用，会病卒，甚见痛惜，殊其门户。
value.en: Sun Quan esteemed him highly but died before promoting him; Quan grieved deeply and honored his kin.
value.literal: Sun Quan deeply prized and favored him; before he could promote him to office he died of illness; Quan greatly mourned and singled out his household for favor.

value.zh: 览子固，字子贱，本名密，避滕密，改作固。
value.en: His son Gu, styled Zijian—born Mi—renamed Gu to avoid Teng Mi's name.
value.literal: Lan's son Gu, courtesy name Zijian, originally named Mi, changed to Gu to avoid Teng Mi.

value.zh: 固在襁褓中，阚泽见而异之，曰：“此兒后必致公辅。”
value.en: Kan Ze peered into his cradle and declared, "This boy will reach the highest councils."
value.literal: While Gu was still in swaddling Kan Ze saw him and marveled, saying: "This child will surely rise to duke or minister."

value.zh: 固少丧父，独与母居，家贫守约，色养致敬，族弟孤弱，与同寒温。
value.en: Gu lost his father young and kept his mother in poverty yet filial ease; he sheltered a helpless cousin as his own.
value.literal: Gu in youth lost his father and lived alone with his mother; the family was poor yet he kept restraint; in supporting her with gentle demeanor he showed utmost respect; a younger male cousin was orphaned and weak, and he shared cold and warmth with him.

value.zh: 翻与固同僚书曰：“丁子贱塞渊好德，堂构克举，野无遗薪，斯之为懿，其美优矣。
value.en: Fan wrote a fellow official: "Ding Zijian is depth and virtue embodied; he raises the family hall without leaving kindling in the field—that is true grace.
value.literal: Fan wrote to a colleague serving with Gu: "Ding Zijian is deep as a spring and loves virtue; the hall's frame is well raised; in the wilds no stray firewood remains—such is his excellence; its beauty is supreme.

value.zh: 令德之后，惟此君嘉耳。”
value.en: Among sons of good stock none shines like him."
value.literal: Among heirs of fine virtue only this gentleman is praiseworthy."

value.zh: 历显位，孙休时固为左御史大夫，孙皓即位，迁司徒。
value.en: He climbed to high office—Left Imperial Clerk under Sun Xiu, Minister of Education once Sun Hao ruled.
value.literal: He rose through eminent posts; under Sun Xiu he became Left Imperial Clerk; when Sun Hao ascended the throne he advanced to Minister of Education.

value.zh: 皓悖虐，固与陆凯、孟宗同心忧国，年七十六卒。
value.en: When Hao turned vicious, Gu joined Lu Kai and Meng Zong in loyal anxiety; he died at seventy-six.
value.literal: Hao was cruel and tyrannical; Gu with Lu Kai and Meng Zong shared one heart worrying for the state; he died at seventy-six sui.

value.zh: 子弥，字钦远，仕晋，至梁州刺史。
value.en: His son Mi, styled Qinyuan, served Jin as Inspector of Liangzhou.
value.literal: His son Mi, courtesy name Qinyuan, served Jin and rose to Inspector of Liangzhou.

value.zh: 孙潭，光禄大夫。
value.en: Grandson Tan became Household Grandee.
value.literal: Grandson Tan, Household Grandee.

value.zh: ◎徐陵字元大，历三县长，所在著称，迁零陵太守。
value.en: ◎ Xu Ling, styled Yuanda, distinguished himself over three magistracies and became prefect of Lingling.
value.literal: ◎ Xu Ling, courtesy name Yuanda, served as magistrate of three counties and was renowned wherever posted; he advanced to Administrator of Lingling.

value.zh: 时朝廷俟以列卿之位，故翻书曰：“元大受上卿之遇，叔向在晋，未若於今。”
value.en: The court meant to give him ministerial rank; Fan wrote, "Yuanda gains honors Shuxiang never saw in Jin."
value.literal: At the time the court awaited him with the seat of a ranked minister; therefore Fan wrote: "Yuanda receives treatment worthy of a senior minister—even Shuxiang in Jin never knew such favor today."

value.zh: 其见重如此。
value.en: Such was the regard he commanded.
value.literal: Thus was he held in such esteem.

value.zh: 陵卒，僮客土田或见侵夺，骆统为陵家讼之，求与丁览、卜清等为比，权许焉。
value.en: After Ling died, creditors preyed on his bondservants and fields; Luo Tong sued for his family and won Sun Quan's nod to match Ding Lan's precedent.
value.literal: When Ling died, retainers and farmland were sometimes seized; Luo Tong pleaded for Ling's household and asked that they be treated like Ding Lan, Bu Qing, and the rest—Quan approved.

value.zh: 陵子平，字伯先，童龀知名，翻甚爱之，屡称叹焉。
value.en: His son Ping, styled Boxian, was a prodigy Yu Fan doted on and praised aloud.
value.literal: Ling's son Ping, courtesy name Boxian, was renowned from childhood; Fan loved him deeply and often praised him.

value.zh: 诸葛恪为丹杨太守，讨山越，以平威重思虑，可与效力，请平为丞，稍迁武昌左部督，倾心接物，士卒皆为尽力。
value.en: Zhuge Ke, campaigning in Danyang, valued Ping's weight of character and took him as aide, then raised him to command Wu's left wing—where Ping won every rank and file heart.
value.literal: Zhuge Ke, as Administrator of Danyang, campaigned against the mountain Yue; deeming Ping grave in bearing and steady in counsel, fit to serve, he requested Ping as assistant magistrate; Ping was gradually promoted to Commander of the Left Wing at Wuchang, treated people with whole heart, and the soldiers all gave their utmost.

value.zh: 初，平为恪从事，意甚薄，及恪辅政，待平益疏。
value.en: Ke had once slighted Ping as a mere clerk; as chief minister he kept him at even greater distance.
value.literal: At first, when Ping served Ke as an aide, Ke thought little of him; once Ke became regent he grew colder toward Ping.

value.zh: 恪被害，子建亡走，为平部曲所得，平使遣去，别为佗军所获。
value.en: Ke's son Jian ran into Ping's troops; Ping sent him on, only for another column to take him.
value.literal: When Ke was assassinated, his son Jian fled and was seized by Ping's retainers; Ping ordered him released, but another unit captured him.

value.zh: 平两妇归宗，敬奉情过乎厚。
value.en: He showed two estranged wives a generosity warmer than ritual required.
value.literal: Ping's two wives returned to their natal clans; he honored them with devotion deeper than ordinary duty.

value.zh: 其行义敦笃，皆此类也。〉
value.en: His integrity ran thick and true—every deed of this stamp.〉
value.literal: His righteous conduct was earnest and steadfast—all of a piece with this.〉

value.zh: 在南十餘年，年七十卒。
value.en: He spent a dozen years in the far south and died at seventy.
value.literal: In the south more than ten years, he died at seventy sui.

value.zh: 〈《吴书》曰：翻虽在徙弃，心不忘国，常忧五谿宜讨，以辽东海绝，听人使来属，尚不足取，今去人财以求马，既非国利，又恐无获。
value.en: 〈The Book of Wu says exile never dimmed Fan's patriotism—he pressed for action in Wuxi, dismissed Liaodong fealty across broken seas, and warned that trading treasure for horses helped nobody.
value.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Though Fan lived in banishment his heart never left the state; he constantly urged that the five gorges of Wuxi deserved a campaign. With the Liaodong sea cut off, even hearing envoys come over to submit was hardly worth the trouble; now to squander our wealth buying horses serves neither the realm nor, he feared, would it succeed.

value.zh: 欲谏不敢，作表以示吕岱，岱不报，为爱憎所白，复徙苍梧猛陵。
value.en: He drafted advice for Lü Dai, heard nothing back, fell victim to slander, and was shifted deeper into Cangwu.
value.literal: He wished to remonstrate but dared not; he drafted a memorial and showed it to Lü Dai, who gave no answer; maligned by petty likes and dislikes, Fan was transferred again to Mengling in Cangwu.

value.zh: 《江表传》曰：后权遣将士至辽东，於海中遭风，多所没失，权悔之，乃令曰：“昔赵简子称诸君之唯唯，不如周舍之谔谔。
value.en: The Jiangbiao zhuan tells how failed Liaodong fleets moved Quan to cite Zhao Jianzi: "flatterers cannot rival one honest Zhou She.
value.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Later Quan dispatched officers to Liaodong; they met storms at sea and many were lost; Quan regretted it and issued an order: "Long ago Zhao Jianzi said a chorus of yes-men is no match for Zhou She's blunt speech.

value.zh: 虞翻亮直，善於尽言，国之周舍也。
value.en: Yu Fan's blunt candor makes him Wu's Zhou She.
value.literal: Yu Fan is candid and straight and excels at speaking his whole mind—he is our Zhou She.

value.zh: 前使翻在此，此役不成。”
value.en: With Fan at court that folly would never have sailed."
value.literal: Had Fan been there on that mission, the expedition would not have miscarried."

value.zh: 促下问交州，翻若尚存者，给其人船，发遣还都；
value.en: He ordered Jiaozhou questioned at once—if Fan lived, send a ship to bring him home;
value.literal: Hasten inquiry to Jiaozhou: if Fan still lives, furnish him a boat and escort him to the capital;

value.zh: 若以亡者，送丧还本郡，使兒子仕宦。
value.en: if he had died, return the coffin and ennoble his sons.
value.literal: if he has died, send his coffin to his native commandery and appoint his sons to office.

value.zh: 会翻已终。〉
value.en: Fan was already gone.〉
value.literal: It happened that Fan had already passed away.〉

value.zh: 翻有十一子。
value.en: Yu Fan fathered eleven sons.
value.literal: Fan had eleven sons.

value.zh: 第四子汜最知名，永安初，從選曹朗為散騎中常侍，後為監軍使者，討扶嚴，病卒，
value.en: Fourth-born Si stood tallest—promoted from Selection clerk to mounted attendant, then died leading troops against Fuyan.
value.literal: The fourth son, Si, was most renowned; at the start of Yong'an he went from Gentleman of the Selection Bureau to Regular Mounted Attendant; later he became Military Supervisor Envoy on the campaign against Fuyan and died of illness.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：汜字世洪，生南海，年十六，父卒，还乡里。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu says Si, styled Shihong, was Nanhai-born and came home at sixteen when his father died.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Si, courtesy name Shihong, was born in Nanhai; at sixteen sui his father died and he returned to his native place.

value.zh: 孙綝废幼主，迎立琅邪王休。
value.en: Sun Lin cast the boy emperor aside for Prince Langye's Sun Xiu.
value.literal: Sun Lin deposed the young ruler and welcomed Prince Langye Wang Xiu to succeed.

value.zh: 休未至，綝欲入宫，图为不轨，召百官会议，皆惶怖失色，徒唯唯而已。
value.en: Lin meant to seize the palace before Xiu arrived; the bureaucrats could only nod, pale.
value.literal: Before Xiu arrived Lin wished to enter the palace and plot treason; he summoned the hundred officials to council—all were terrified and bloodless, uttering only yes-yes.

value.zh: 汜对曰：“明公为国伊周，处将相之位，擅废立之威，将上安宗庙，下惠百姓，大小踊跃，自以伊霍复见。
value.en: "Si told Lin he played Yi Yin to the realm—why panic the court by rushing the harem?
value.literal: Si answered: "You, enlightened lord, stand as Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou for the state; you hold general and minister rank and wield power to depose and enthrone—you will pacify the ancestral shrines above and bless the hundred surnames below; great and small leap with joy, each imagining Yi Yin and Huo Guang reborn.

value.zh: 今迎王未至，而欲入宫，如是，群下摇荡，众听疑惑，非所以永终忠孝，扬名后世也。”
value.en: Entering the palace early would shake faith and stain his fame."
value.literal: Now the king you welcome has not arrived yet you wish to enter the palace—in this way subordinates waver and the multitude listens in doubt—it is no way to secure loyalty and filial piety forever or lift your name for later ages."

value.zh: 綝不怿，竟立休。
value.en: Lin sulked yet crowned Xiu.
value.literal: Lin was displeased but in the end enthroned Xiu.

value.zh: 休初即位，汜与贺邵、王蕃、薛莹俱为散骑中常侍。
value.en: Xiu kept Si, He Shao, Wang Fan, and Xue Ying as close attendants.
value.literal: When Xiu first ascended, Si served with He Shao, Wang Fan, and Xue Ying as Regular Mounted Attendants.

value.zh: 以讨扶严功拜交州刺史、冠军将军、餘姚侯，寻卒。〉
value.en: Fuyan won him Jiaozhou, the Champion baton, and Yuyan marquisate—then death.〉
value.literal: For merit in the Fuyan campaign he was appointed Inspector of Jiaozhou, Champion General, and Marquis of Yuyao; soon afterward he died.〉

value.zh: 汜弟忠，宜都太守。
value.en: Younger brother Zhong governed Yidu.
value.literal: Si's younger brother Zhong was Administrator of Yidu.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：忠字世方，翻第五子。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu gives Zhong as Fan's fifth son, styled Shifang.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Zhong, courtesy name Shifang, was Fan's fifth son.

value.zh: 贞固幹事，好识人物，造吴郡陆机於童龀之年，称上虞魏迁於无名之初，终皆远致，为著闻之士。
value.en: Zhong spotted Lu Ji as a boy and Wei Qian before fame—both climbed high.
value.literal: Chaste, firm, capable in affairs, skilled at recognizing men—he sought out Lu Ji of Wu commandery while still in childhood and praised Wei Qian of Shangyu before he had a name; both in the end rose far and became scholars of recorded fame.

value.zh: 交同县王岐於孤宦之族，仕进先至宜都太守，忠乃代之。
value.en: He bonded with clerk-born Wang Qi—Qi held Yidu first, Zhong followed.
value.literal: He befriended Wang Qi of the same county from a clan of orphaned clerks; Wang advanced first to Administrator of Yidu, and Zhong succeeded him.

value.zh: 晋征吴，忠与夷道监陆晏、晏弟中夏督景坚守不下，城溃被害。
value.en: Yu Zhong died defending Yidao beside Lu Yan and Lu Jing when Jin breached the walls.
value.literal: When Jin campaigned against Wu, Zhong with Yidao intendant Lu Yan and Yan's younger brother Central Summer Commander Lu Jing held firm and would not yield; when the city broke they were killed.

value.zh: 忠子谭，字思奥。
value.en: His son Tan styled Si'ao.
value.literal: Zhong's son Tan, courtesy name Si'ao.

value.zh: 《晋阳秋》称谭清贞有检操，外如退弱，内坚正有胆幹。
value.en: The Jinyang qiu calls Tan reserved yet steel inside—soft-spoken but unbending.
value.literal: The Jinyang qiu praises Tan as chaste and restrained with disciplined integrity—outwardly seeming yielding and weak, inwardly firm, upright, and bold in capacity.

value.zh: 仕晋，历位内外，终於卫将军，追赠侍中左光禄大夫，开府仪同三司。〉
value.en: Under Jin he reached Defender-in-Chief and won posthumous ministerial glory.〉
value.literal: He served Jin, rose through inner and outer posts, ending as Defender-in-Chief—posthumously honored Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee with Office Equal to the Three Dukes.〉

value.zh: 聳，越騎校尉。
value.en: Yu Song served as Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
value.literal: Song was Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

value.zh: 累遷廷尉，湘東、河間太守；
value.en: He rose to Commandant of Justice and prefect of Xiangdong and Hejian;
value.literal: He was promoted in stages to Commandant of Justice, Administrator of Xiangdong and Hejian;

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：耸字世龙，翻第六子也。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu names Song as Fan's sixth son, styled Shilong.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Song, courtesy name Shilong, was Fan's sixth son.

value.zh: 清虚无欲，进退以礼，在吴历清官，入晋，除河间相，王素闻耸名，厚敬礼之。
value.en: Ascetic and punctilious in Wu, he became Hejian chancellor under Jin; Prince Su honored his reputation.
value.literal: Clear, empty of desire, advancing and retreating by ritual—in Wu he passed through pure offices; entering Jin he was appointed Chancellor of Hejian; Prince Su long hearing Song's name treated him with thick courtesy and respect.

value.zh: 耸抽引人物，务在幽隐孤陋之中。
value.en: He insisted on lifting talent from hedgerows and hovels.
value.literal: Song drew forth men of affairs, striving for those hidden in obscurity, orphaned and lowly.

value.zh: 时王岐难耸，以高士所达，必合秀异，耸书与族子察曰：“世之取士，曾不招未齿於丘园，索良才於总猥，所誉依已成，所毁依已败，此吾所以叹息也。”
value.en: "Wang Qi argued great names imply genius; Song answered his kinsman Cha that patronage chases winners and shuns unknowns—a vice worth mourning."
value.literal: At the time Wang Qi challenged Song: men of lofty repute reach only the outstandingly gifted; Song wrote his clansman Cha: "This age's recruitment never summons the toothless recluse from grove and garden nor seeks fine talent from the crude crowd; praise follows what is already made, slander tracks what is already ruined—that is why I sigh."

value.zh: 耸疾俗丧祭无度，弟昺卒，祭以少牢，酒饭而已，当时族党并遵行之。〉
value.en: He trimmed funeral feasts to wine and grain when Bing died, and kin copied him.〉
value.literal: Song loathed vulgar excess in mourning sacrifices; when younger brother Bing died he offered only the lesser beast sacrifice—wine and rice—and kinsmen alike followed the rule.〉

value.zh: 昺，廷尉尚書，濟陰太守。
value.en: Bing rose to ministerial rank and governed Jiyin.
value.literal: Bing was Minister of Justice and Minister over the Masses, Administrator of Jiyin.

value.zh: 〈会稽典录曰：昺字世文，翻第八子也。
value.en: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu records Bing, Fan's eighth son, styled Shiwen.
value.literal: 〈The Kuaiji dianlu states: Bing, courtesy name Shiwen, was Fan's eighth son.

value.zh: 少有倜傥之志，仕吴黄门郎，以捷对见异，超拜尚书侍中。
value.en: Wu valued his wit at the Yellow Gates and jumped him to palace minister.
value.literal: In youth he cherished a free hero's ambition; serving Wu as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates he was singled out for quick repartee and vaulted to Palace Attendant Minister.

value.zh: 晋军来伐，遣昺持节都督武昌已上诸军事，昺先上还节盖印绶，然后归顺。
value.en: Facing invasion Bing surrendered credentials above Wuchang before yielding.
value.literal: When Jin's army came to strike he dispatched Bing with tally as Area Commander-in-Chief for all military affairs from Wuchang upward; Bing first returned tally, canopy, seals and ribbons, then submitted.

value.zh: 在济阴，抑强扶弱，甚著威风。〉
value.en: At Jiyin he humbled bullies and shielded commoners—justice visible on the street.〉
value.literal: In Jiyin he checked the mighty and aided the weak—his martial awe stood renowned.〉

value.zh: 孫登字子高，權長子也。
value.en: Sun Deng, whose courtesy name was Zigao, was Sun Quan's firstborn son.
value.literal: Sun Deng, courtesy name Zigao, was the eldest son of Sun Quan.

value.zh: 魏黃初二年，以權爲吳王，拜登東中郎將，封萬戶侯，登辭疾不受。
value.en: In 221, the Wei court invested Sun Quan as King of Wu and named Sun Deng General of the Household for All Purposes of the East with a fief of ten thousand households; Sun Deng pleaded ill health and refused the appointment and title.
value.literal: In the second year of Huangchu of Wei, Sun Quan was made King of Wu; Sun Deng was appointed General of the Household for All Purposes of the East and enfeoffed as marquis of ten thousand households, but Sun Deng declined citing illness and did not accept.

value.zh: 是歲，立登爲太子，選置師傅，銓簡秀士，以爲賔友，於是諸葛恪、張休、顧譚、陳表等以選入，侍講詩書，出從騎射。
value.en: The same year Sun Deng was made crown prince. Tutors were appointed and talented men chosen as his companions, so Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, Chen Biao, and others joined his household by competitive selection—indoors they expounded the Classics; outdoors they rode and shot with him.
value.literal: That year he was established as heir apparent; masters and tutors were chosen and set in place, and outstanding scholars were screened and selected to be guests and companions; thereupon Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, Chen Biao, and others entered by selection, lecturing him on the Classics and histories indoors and accompanying him in riding and archery when he went out.

value.zh: 權欲登讀《漢書》，習知近代之事，以張昭有師法，重煩勞之，乃令休從昭受讀，還以授登。
value.en: Sun Quan wanted his heir to read the Han shu and learn recent history. Zhang Zhao was the acknowledged master teacher, but Sun Quan hesitated to burden him, so he had Zhang Xiu study under Zhang Zhao and then pass the lessons on to Sun Deng.
value.literal: Sun Quan wished Sun Deng to read the Han shu and become familiar with affairs of recent times; because Zhang Zhao had proper methods of instruction and Sun Quan shrank from wearying him excessively, he ordered Zhang Xiu to receive instruction in reading from Zhang Zhao and return to teach Sun Deng.

value.zh: 登待接寮屬，略用布衣之禮，與恪、休、譚等或同輿而載，或共帳而寐。
value.en: With his staff Sun Deng kept to plain, almost commoner-level courtesy: he shared a carriage with Zhuge Ke, Zhang Xiu, Gu Tan, and the like, or slept in the same tent with them.
value.literal: In receiving his subordinate officials Sun Deng broadly used the rites of a commoner, and with Ke, Xiu, Tan, and others he sometimes rode in the same carriage or slept in the same tent.

value.zh: 太傅張溫言於權曰：「夫中庶子官最親密，切問近對，宜用儁德。」
value.en: Grand Tutor Zhang Wen urged Sun Quan: "Palace attendants stand closest to the heir; they field urgent questions at his side. The posts demand men of exceptional moral stature."
value.literal: Grand Tutor Zhang Wen spoke to Sun Quan, saying: "The office of palace attendant is the most intimate; it answers pressing questions at close quarters; outstanding virtue ought to be employed."

value.zh: 於是乃用表等爲中庶子。
value.en: Sun Quan then appointed Chen Biao and others palace attendants.
value.literal: Thereupon Chen Biao and others were employed as palace attendants.

value.zh: 後又以庶子禮拘，復令整巾侍坐。
value.en: Later the formal etiquette for attendants proved awkwardly stiff, so he told them to straighten their caps and take seats while on duty.
value.literal: Later, because the rites for palace attendants were restrictive, he again ordered them to arrange their headcloths and attend seated.

value.zh: 黃龍元年，權稱尊號，登爲皇太子，以恪爲左輔，休右弼，譚爲輔正，表爲翼正都尉，是爲四友，而謝景、范慎、刁玄、羊衜等皆爲賔客，
value.en: In 229 Sun Quan took the imperial style; Sun Deng became crown prince. Zhuge Ke was named left support, Zhang Xiu right support, Gu Tan rectifier of the heir, and Chen Biao capital commandant who wings the rectifier—the group known as the Four Friends—while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Diao Xuan, Yang Dao, and others served as his guests.
value.literal: In the first year of Huanglong, when Sun Quan assumed the exalted title, Sun Deng became imperial heir; Ke was made left support, Xiu right support, Tan rectifier of the heir, Biao capital commandant who wings the rectifier—these were called the Four Friends—while Xie Jing, Fan Shen, Diao Xuan, Yang Dao, and others all became guests,

value.zh: 〈衜音道。〉
value.en: 〈The gloss reads the character with the same sound as dao, 'way.'〉
value.literal: 〈The note glosses the character as pronounced dao, like the word for 'way."

value.zh: 於是東宮號爲多士。
value.en: The heir's establishment was soon renowned for the density of talent around him.
value.literal: Thereupon the Eastern Palace was styled as abounding in worthy men.

value.zh: 〈《吳錄》曰：慎字孝敬，廣陵人，竭忠知己之君，纏綿三益之友，時人榮之。
value.en: 〈According to the Wu lu, Fan Shen, styled Xiaojing, came from Guangling. He gave his whole loyalty to a sovereign who truly knew him, and he clung to friendships that enriched character in the classical "three ways"—contemporaries held him in high esteem. )
value.literal: 〈The Wu lu states: Fan, courtesy name Xiaojing, was a man of Guangling; he exhausted loyalty toward a ruler who knew him, and clung to friends who brought the three benefits; people of the time honored him for it. )

value.zh: 著論二十篇，名曰《矯非》。
value.en: He wrote twenty essays collected under the title Rectifying Error.
value.literal: He composed twenty treatises, entitled Rectifying Error.

value.zh: 後爲侍中，出補武昌左部督，治軍整頓。
value.en: He later served as palace attendant, then transferred to command the left wing at Wuchang, where he ran a tight, disciplined camp.
value.literal: Later he became palace attendant, went out to fill the post of commander of the left division at Wuchang, and governed the army in good order.

value.zh: 孫皓移都，甚憚之，詔曰：「慎勳德俱茂，朕所敬憑，宜登上公，以副衆望。」
value.en: After Sun Hao shifted the capital he grew wary of Fan Shen's stature and issued an edict: "Fan's achievements and character alike command respect; I lean on him with reverence. He should be raised to the highest ducal rank to satisfy public expectation."
value.literal: When Sun Hao moved the capital he greatly feared him and issued an edict saying: "Fan's merit and virtue are both flourishing; he is one on whom We rely in reverence; he ought to be raised to the highest duke rank to answer the hopes of the multitude."

value.zh: 以爲太尉。
value.en: He was appointed grand commandant.
value.literal: He was made grand commandant.

value.zh: 慎自恨久爲將，遂託老耄。
value.en: Fan Shen had wearied of life in the field and pleaded senility to step down.
value.literal: Fan Shen himself resented having long been a general and therefore pleaded extreme old age.

value.zh: 軍士戀之，舉營爲之隕涕。
value.en: The troops loved him; an entire camp shed tears at his departure.
value.literal: The soldiers were attached to him; the whole camp wept tears for him.

value.zh: 鳳凰三年卒，子耀嗣。
value.en: He died in 274; his son Fan Yao inherited his rank.
value.literal: He died in the third year of Fenghuang; his son Yao succeeded.

value.zh: 玄，丹楊人。
value.en: Diao Xuan was from Danyang.
value.literal: Xuan was a man of Danyang.

value.zh: 衜，南陽人。
value.en: Yang Dao came from Nanyang.
value.literal: Dao was a man of Nanyang.

value.zh: 《吳書》曰：衜初爲中庶子，年二十。
value.en: The Wu shu records that Yang Dao began as a palace attendant at the age of twenty.
value.literal: The Wu shu states: Dao at first was a palace attendant; he was twenty years of age.

value.zh: 時廷尉監隱蕃交結豪傑，自衞將軍全琮等皆傾心敬待，惟衜及宣詔郎豫章楊迪拒絕不與通，時人咸怪之。
value.en: The court jailer Yin Fan was courting powerful men, and even Guard General Quan Zong courted his favor—yet Yang Dao and the edict herald Yang Di of Yuzhang would have nothing to do with him, which contemporaries found inexplicable.
value.literal: At that time the jail overseer of the commandant of justice, Yin Fan, cultivated ties with bold spirits; from Guard General Quan Zong downward all inclined their hearts and treated him with respect; only Dao and the edict announcer of Yuzhang, Yang Di, refused and would not associate with him; people of the time all thought it strange.

value.zh: 而蕃後叛逆，衆乃服之。
value.en: When Yin Fan later turned traitor, everyone conceded that Yang Dao and Yang Di had been right.
value.literal: But when Fan later rebelled, the crowd then admired them.

value.zh: 《江表傳》曰：登使侍中胡綜作賔友目曰：「英才卓越，超踰倫匹，則諸葛恪。
value.en: The Jiangbiao zhuan says Sun Deng had Palace Attendant Hu Zong draft appraisals of his companions: "For brilliance that towers above ordinary men, there is Zhuge Ke.
value.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Deng ordered Palace Attendant Hu Zong to compose a catalogue of guests and companions, saying: "In outstanding talent that transcends the common run, surpassing peers, there is Zhuge Ke.

value.zh: 精識時機，達幽究微，則顧譚。
value.en: For sharp judgment of timing and insight into hidden motives, there is Gu Tan.
value.literal: In keen perception of the opportune moment, penetrating the obscure and investigating the subtle, there is Gu Tan.

value.zh: 凝辨宏達，言能釋結，則謝景。
value.en: For steady judgment, breadth of mind, and words that untangle dilemmas, there is Xie Jing.
value.literal: In concentrated discernment and breadth of vision, in speech able to unravel knots, there is Xie Jing.

value.zh: 究學甄微，游夏同科，則范慎。」
value.en: For scholarship that sifts the fine points and rivals the disciples You and Xia, there is Fan Shen."
value.literal: In exhaustive study and discrimination of the subtle, on a par with You and Xia, there is Fan Shen."

value.zh: 衜乃私駁綜曰：「元遜才而疏，子嘿精而狠，叔發辯而浮，孝敬深而狹。」
value.en: Yang Dao quietly contradicted Hu Zong: "Zhuge Ke is gifted but careless; Gu Tan is sharp but ruthless; Xie Jing is fluent but shallow; Fan Shen is deep but narrow-minded."
value.literal: Dao then privately refuted Zong, saying: "Yuanxun has talent but is careless; Zimo is acute but harsh; Shufa is eloquent but shallow; Xiaojing is profound but narrow."

value.zh: 所言皆有指趣。
value.en: Each remark had a clear point behind it.
value.literal: What he said all had pointed significance.

value.zh: 而衜卒以此言見咎，不爲恪等所親。
value.en: Those words earned Yang Dao resentment, and Zhuge Ke's circle never warmed to him.
value.literal: But Dao in the end because of these words incurred blame and was not treated as intimate by Ke and the others.

value.zh: 後四人皆敗，吳人謂衜之言有徵。
value.en: When all four later fell, Wu observers said Yang Dao's verdicts had proved prophetic.
value.literal: Later when the four men all met ruin, the people of Wu said Dao's words had been verified.

value.zh: 位至桂陽太守，卒。〉
value.en: He rose to prefect of Guiyang and died there.〉
value.literal: He rose to the rank of administrator of Guiyang and died.〉

value.zh: 孫休立，封和子皓爲烏程侯，自新都之本國。
value.en: When Sun Xiu took the throne he enfeoffed Sun He's son Sun Hao as marquis of Wucheng, who traveled from Xindu to his fief.
value.literal: When Sun Xiu was established, he enfeoffed He's son Hao as marquis of Wucheng, who went from Xindu to his own state.

value.zh: 休薨，皓即阼，其年追謚父和曰文皇帝，改葬明陵，置園邑二百家，令、丞奉守。
value.en: After Sun Xiu died Sun Hao succeeded; the same year he posthumously titled his father Sun He as Emperor Wen, reinterred him at Ming Mausoleum with a two-hundred-household funerary estate under magistrate and assistant.
value.literal: When Xiu died, Hao succeeded to the throne; that year he posthumously honored his father He with the title Emperor Wen, reburied him at Ming Mausoleum, established a park settlement of two hundred households, and ordered a magistrate and assistant to maintain guardianship.

value.zh: 後年正月，又分吳郡、丹楊九縣爲吳興郡，治烏程，置太守，四時奉祠。
value.en: The next New Year he carved nine counties from Wu and Danyang into a new Wu Xing commandery based at Wucheng, appointed a grand administrator, and ordered sacrifices each season.
value.literal: In the first month of the following year, again he divided nine counties of Wu commandery and Danyang to make Wu Xing commandery, with its seat at Wucheng, and established a grand administrator, with seasonal sacrifice in the four seasons.

value.zh: 有司奏言，宜立廟京邑。
value.en: Officials memorialized for an ancestral temple in the capital.
value.literal: The responsible officials submitted saying that a temple ought to be established in the capital city.

value.zh: 寶鼎二年七月，使守大匠薛珝營立寢堂，號曰清廟。
value.en: In the seventh month of 267 he had Guardian Grand Engineer Xue Xu build a spirit hall styled the Pure Temple.
value.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Baoding, he ordered the Guardian Grand Engineer Xue Xu to build a hall for the resting spirit, styled the Pure Temple.

value.zh: 十二月，遣守丞相孟仁、太常姚信等備官寮中軍步騎二千人，以靈輿法駕，東迎神於明陵。
value.en: In the twelfth month he sent Acting Chancellor Meng Ren, Grand Master Yao Xin, a full retinue, and two thousand guards with the imperial bier east to Ming Mausoleum to fetch the spirit.
value.literal: In the twelfth month he sent Acting Chancellor Meng Ren, Grand Master of Ceremonies Yao Xin, and others with full complement of officials and followers, two thousand foot and horse of the central army, with the spirit carriage and statutory equipage, to go east and welcome the spirit at Ming Mausoleum.

value.zh: 皓引見仁，親拜送於庭。
value.en: Sun Hao received Meng Ren in audience and bowed him off in the courtyard himself.
value.literal: Hao led Ren in audience and personally bowed in sending off at the courtyard.

value.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：比仁還，中使手詔，日夜相繼，奉問神靈起居動止。
value.en: 〈The Wu shu says that while Meng Ren was returning, couriers with the emperor's own edicts followed one another night and day asking after the spirit's progress.
value.literal: 〈The Wu shu states: When Ren returned, inner envoys with autograph edicts succeeded one another day and night, conveying inquiries after the spirit's rest and rise, movement and stillness.

value.zh: 巫覡言見和被服，顏色如平生日，皓悲喜涕淚，悉召公卿尚書詣闕門下受賜。〉
value.en: Mediums claimed Sun He appeared in court dress, his face as in life; Sun Hao wept for joy and sorrow and summoned the high ministers to the gate to receive blessings.〉
value.literal: Witches and shamans said they saw He in robes and caps, his complexion as on ordinary days of life; Hao was moved between joy and sorrow to tears and mucus, and summoned all dukes, ministers, and directors of departments to the gates below the palace to receive bestowal.〉

value.zh: 靈輿當至，使丞相陸凱奉三牲祭於近郊，皓於金城外露宿。
value.en: As the bier neared, he told Chancellor Lu Kai to sacrifice the three victims in the near suburb while he himself camped in the open outside the Metal Wall.
value.literal: When the spirit carriage was about to arrive, he ordered Chancellor Lu Kai to offer the three sacrificial victims in sacrifice at the near suburbs, while Hao lodged in the open outside the Metal Wall.

value.zh: 明日，望拜於東門之外。
value.en: The next day he bowed toward the east outside the city gate.
value.literal: The next day he gazed and bowed outside the eastern gate.

value.zh: 其翌日，拜廟薦祭，歔欷悲感。
value.en: The following day he worshiped at the temple, offered sacrifice, and wept aloud.
value.literal: The day after that he bowed in the temple, presented sacrifice, sighed and wept, moved and grieved.

value.zh: 比七日三祭，倡技晝夜娛樂。
value.en: For seven days and three services, musicians and dancers entertained without cease.
value.literal: For seven days with three sacrifices, singing girls and performers by day and night provided entertainment.

value.zh: 有司奏言「祭不欲數，數則黷，宜以禮斷情」，然後止。
value.en: The responsible officials memorialized, "Sacrifices should not be too frequent; if they are frequent, they become profane. Emotion should be restrained by ritual." Only then did the observances stop.
value.literal: The responsible officials submitted saying "Sacrifice ought not to be frequent; if frequent then it is profane; one ought to cut off feeling by ritual"—only then did it stop.

value.zh: 〈《吳歷》曰：和四子：皓、德、謙、俊。
value.en: 〈The Wu li lists four sons of Sun He: Sun Hao, Sun De, Sun Qian, and Sun Jun.
value.literal: 〈The Wu li states: He had four sons: Hao, De, Qian, and Jun.

value.zh: 孫休即位，封德錢唐侯，謙永安侯，俊拜騎都尉。
value.en: When Sun Xiu came to the throne he enfeoffed Sun De at Qiantang, Sun Qian at Yongan, and appointed Sun Jun cavalry commandant.
value.literal: When Sun Xiu assumed the throne, he enfeoffed De as marquis of Qiantang, Qian as marquis of Yongan, and Jun was appointed cavalry commandant.

value.zh: 皓在武昌，吳興施但因民之不堪命，聚萬餘人，劫謙，將至秣陵，欲立之。
value.en: While Sun Hao was at Wuchang, Shi Dan of Wu Xing, claiming the people could not endure his rule, raised over ten thousand men, seized Sun Qian, and marched on Moling intending to enthrone him.
value.literal: When Hao was at Wuchang, Shi Dan of Wu Xing, because the people could not bear their commands, gathered more than ten thousand men, seized Qian, and was about to reach Moling, intending to establish him.

value.zh: 未至三十里住，擇吉日，但遣使以謙命詔丁固、諸葛靚。
value.en: They halted thirty li short, picked an auspicious day, and sent envoys in Sun Qian's name to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.
value.literal: Before reaching thirty li they halted, chose an auspicious day, and Dan sent envoys with Qian's order to summon Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing.

value.zh: 靚即斬其使。
value.en: Zhuge Jing beheaded the messenger at once.
value.literal: Jing thereupon beheaded his envoy.

value.zh: 但遂前到九里，固、靚出擊，大破之。
value.en: Shi Dan pushed on to Jiuli; Ding Gu and Zhuge Jing sallied forth and crushed him.
value.literal: Dan thereupon advanced to Jiuli; Gu and Jing came out and attacked, greatly defeating him.

value.zh: 但兵裸身無鎧甲，臨陣皆披散。
value.en: Shi Dan's soldiers were naked, without armor; when they faced the battle line they all scattered.
value.literal: Dan's soldiers were naked without armor; facing battle they all scattered.

value.zh: 謙獨坐車中，遂生獲之。
value.en: Sun Qian alone sat in a carriage and was taken alive.
value.literal: Qian alone sat in a carriage; thereupon he was captured alive.

value.zh: 固不敢殺，以狀告皓，皓酖之，母子皆死。
value.en: Ding Gu dared not execute him and reported to Sun Hao, who poisoned him with wine; mother and son both died.
value.literal: Gu did not dare kill him but reported the situation to Hao; Hao poisoned him with ale, and mother and son both died.

value.zh: 俊，張承外孫，聦明辨惠，爲遠近所稱，皓又殺之。〉
value.en: Sun Jun was Zhang Cheng's grandson by a daughter—clever and praised far and wide—and Sun Hao killed him too.〉
value.literal: Jun was Zhang Cheng's maternal grandson, clever in discrimination and quick in wisdom, praised by far and near, and Hao again killed him.〉

value.zh: 諸葛恪
value.en: Zhuge Ke
value.literal: Zhuge Ke.

value.zh: 於是亮、峻聽恪故吏斂葬，遂求之於石子岡。
value.en: The regents let old aides recover Ke from Shizi Gang.
value.literal: Thereupon Liang and Jun allowed Ke’s former clerks to wrap him for burial and sought the corpse at Shizi Ridge.

value.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：朝臣有乞為恪立碑以銘其勳績者，博士盛衝以為不應。
value.en: 〈Some wanted a monument—Doctor Sheng Chong refused.
value.literal: 〈The Jiang Biao Zhuan says: Courtiers petitioned to raise a stele engraving Ke’s deeds—Doctor Sheng Chong argued against.

value.zh: 孫休曰：「盛夏出軍，士卒傷損，無尺寸之功，不可謂能；
value.en: Sun Xiu judged: “Summer war without gain is not skill;
value.literal: Sun Xiu said: “To march midsummer wounding troops without inch-wide merit—cannot be called able;

value.zh: 受託孤之任，死於豎子之手，不可謂智。
value.en: to die regent at a stripling’s blade is not wisdom.
value.literal: to bear orphan-entrustment yet die at a boy’s hand—cannot be called wise.

value.zh: 衝議為是。」
value.en: Sheng Chong had the right of it."
value.literal: Chong’s opinion was correct."

value.zh: 遂寢。〉
value.en: The stele died unraised.〉
value.literal: Thereupon the matter slept.〉

value.zh: 典軍施正勸綝徵立琅邪王休，綝從之。
value.en: Shi Zheng talked Lin into king Huima—Sun Xiu.
value.literal: Army Clerk Shi Zheng urged Lin summon and enthrone Prince Langye Xiu—Lin followed.

value.zh: 遣宗正楷奉書於休曰：
value.en: Sun Kai carried summons to Xiu:
value.literal: Dispatched Director of Imperial Clan Kai bearing letter to Xiu saying:

value.zh: 綝以薄才，見授大任，不能輔導陛下。
value.en: The indictment opens with Lin’s sham confession that he failed as regent.
value.literal: Lin by slender talent received great charge—unable to tutor guidance Your Majesty.

value.zh: 頃月以來，多所造立。
value.en: It lists Liang’s alleged novelty-building excesses.
value.literal: These recent months—many creations established.

value.zh: 親近劉承，悅於美色；
value.en: Charges dalliance with Liu Cheng and palace women.
value.literal: Favored Liu Cheng—delighted in beauty;

value.zh: 發吏民婦女，料其好者，留於宮內，取兵弟十八已下三千餘人，習之苑中，連日續夜，大小呼嗟，敗壞藏中矛戈五千餘枚，以作戲具。
value.en: Monstrous catalog of Liang’s alleged orgies and toy navy.
value.literal: Drafted civilian women—grading fairest—detained inside palace—recruited soldier youths eighteen and below over three thousand—drilled them in park—days linked nights—great and small wailed—ruined armory spears and halberds over five thousand—fashioned play gear.

value.zh: 朱據先帝舊臣，子男熊、損皆承父之基，以忠議自立，昔殺小主。
value.en: Claims Zhu heirs murdered princess—distorts truth.
value.literal: Zhu Ju prior emperor old minister—sons Xiong and Sun both inherited father base—stood by loyal counsel—yet killed junior lord.

value.zh: 自是大主所創，帝不復精其本未，便殺熊、損，諫不見用。
value.en: Blames Liang for Zhu executions without hearing Lin’s guilt.
value.literal: Since then Great Princess authored affair—emperor never examined root tip—then slew Xiong and Sun—remonstrance unused.

value.zh: 諸下莫不側息。
value.en: Court terrified into silence.
value.literal: Underlings none failed to hold breath.

value.zh: 帝於宮中作小船三百餘艘，成以金銀，師工晝夜不息。
value.en: Accuses toy fleet waste.
value.literal: Emperor inside palace built small boats over three hundred—gold and silver clad—artisans day night ceaseless.

value.zh: 太常全尚，累世受恩，不能督諸宗親，而全端等委城就魏。
value.en: Smears Quan clan treason.
value.literal: Chamberlain Quan Shang—generations receiving grace—unable to supervise clan kin—while Quan Duan and others surrendered cities to Wei.

value.zh: 尚位過重，曾無一言以諫陛下，而與敵往來，使傳國消息，懼必傾危社稷。
value.en: Claims Quan Shang spied for Wei.
value.literal: Shang rank overly weighty—never one word remonstrating Majesty—yet trafficked with foe—transmitting state messages—I fear certain overturn of altars.

value.zh: 推案舊典，運集大王，輒以今月二十七日擒尚斬承。
value.en: Announces staged arrests— date fixed.
value.literal: Pushing investigation old precedent—fortune gathers Great King—therefore twenty-seventh of this month seized Shang executed Cheng.

value.zh: 以帝為會稽王，遣楷牽迎。
value.en: Deposes Liang to Kuaiji prince—sends escort for Xiu.
value.literal: Demoting emperor Prince of Kuaiji—dispatching Kai escorting welcome.

value.zh: 百寮喁喁。
value.en: Bureaucracy voiced obedience.
value.literal: Hundred officials murmured assent.

value.zh: 立任道側。
value.en: They lined the route for new sovereign.
value.literal: Stood waiting along roadway.

value.zh: 綝奉牛酒詣休，休不受，齎詣左將軍張布。
value.en: Sun Lin’s peace gifts went to Zhang Bu—Xiu declined face-to-face.
value.literal: Lin carried cattle wine visiting Xiu—Xiu refused—had them forwarded to General of the Left Zhang Bu.

value.zh: 酒酣，出怨言曰：「徹廢少主時，多勸吾自為之者。
value.en: Wine heated—bitter words emerged—“When we utterly deposed young sovereign—many urged me take throne myself.
value.literal: Wine heated—bitter words emerged—“When we utterly deposed young sovereign—many urged me take throne myself.

value.zh: 吾以陛下賢明，故迎之。
value.en: Claims he chose Xiu for virtue.
value.literal: I deemed Your Majesty sagely enlightened—therefore welcomed you.

value.zh: 帝非我不立，今上禮見拒，是與凡臣無異，當復改圖耳。」
value.en: Emperor without me would not stand—now courtesy visit refused—no different from common minister—must scheme anew.”
value.literal: Emperor without me would not stand—now courtesy visit refused—no different from common minister—must scheme anew.”

value.zh: 布以言聞休，休銜之。
value.en: Zhang Bu warned Xiu—resentment seeded.
value.literal: Bu reported speech to Xiu—Xiu nursed grudge.

value.zh: 鞏其有變，數加賞賜，又復加恩侍中，與綝分省文書。
value.en: Emperor Xiu feared Lin would bolt—showered honors and busywork to watch him.
value.literal: Fearing he might stir change—the received character here is probably a scribal error for fear—repeatedly piled rewards—again extended grace as Palace Attendant—sharing Lin province over documents.

value.zh: 或有告綝懷怨侮上欲圖反者，休執以付綝，綝殺之。
value.en: Xiu fed Lin a false informer—Lin killed him—proving brutality.
value.literal: Someone reported Lin nursed grievance insulting superior plotting revolt—Xiu seized accuser handing to Lin—Lin slew him.

value.zh: 由是愈懼，因孟宗求出屯武昌，休許焉，盡敕所督中營精兵萬餘人，皆令裝載，所取武庫兵器，咸令給與。
value.en: Lin fled toward Wuchang with elite ten thousand—throne armed him freely.
value.literal: Thereby Lin grew more fearful—through Meng Zong begged posting garrison Wuchang—Xiu permitted—full order to crack troops over ten thousand he commanded—all directed loaded—armory weapons requested—all granted.

value.zh: 〈《吳曆》曰：綝求中書兩郎，典知荊州諸軍事，主者奏中書不應外出，休特聽之，其所請求，一皆給與。〉
value.en: 〈Wu li: Xiu let Lin pick secretaries for Jingzhou staff.〉
value.literal: 〈Wu li states: Lin begged two Secretariat gentlemen managing Jingzhou military affairs—chief memorialized Secretariat ought not post outward—Xiu specially permitted—all requests granted.〉

value.zh: 將軍魏邈說休曰「綝居外必有變」，武衛士施朔又告「綝欲反有徵」休密問張布，布與丁奉謀於會殺綝。
value.en: General Wei Miao advised Sun Xiu, “If Lin remains outside, there will surely be trouble.” Palace guardsman Shi Shuo also reported, “There are signs that Lin intends rebellion.” Xiu secretly questioned Zhang Bu, and Bu plotted with Ding Feng to kill Lin at the banquet.
value.literal: General Wei Mi advised Xiu—“Lin abroad certain brings mutiny”—Palace guardsman Shi Shuo again reported—“Lin plots revolt with signs”—Xiu secretly questioned Zhang Bu—Bu with Ding Feng plotted banquet killing Lin.

value.zh: 綝死時年二十八。
value.en: Sun Lin perished at twenty-eight.
value.literal: Lin died aged twenty-eight.

value.zh: 休耽與峻、綝同族，特除其屬籍，稱之曰故峻、故綝雲​​。
value.en: Emperor Xiu struck Sun Jun and Sun Lin from the imperial lineage—only “the late Jun” and “the late Lin” remained on the record.
value.literal: Xiu was ashamed to share a clan with Jun and Lin, so he specially removed them from the clan registers and referred to them as “the late Jun” and “the late Lin,” it is said.

value.zh: 休又下詔曰：「諸葛恪、滕胤、呂據蓋以無罪為峻、綝兄弟所見殘害，可為痛心，促皆改葬，各為祭奠。
value.en: Sun Xiu further issued an edict: “Zhuge Ke, Teng Yin, and Lü Ju were all innocent, yet they were cruelly murdered by the brothers Jun and Lin. This is heartbreaking. Hurry to rebury them all properly, and provide sacrifices for each.
value.literal: Xiu further issued edict: “Zhuge Ke, Teng Yin, and Lü Ju were innocent yet slaughtered by Jun and Lin brothers—utterly heartbreaking—hasten reburial for each with sacrifices.

value.zh: 其罹恪等事見遠徙者，一切召還。」
value.en: As for those implicated in the affairs of Ke and the others and sent into distant exile, summon them all back.”
value.literal: Those who suffered Ke affair and were banished afar—summon all back.”

value.zh: 永安三年，都尉嚴密建丹楊湖田，作浦裡塘。
value.en: Yongan 3: Yan Mi pitched the Puli reclamation on Danyang’s lakes.
value.literal: Third year of Yongan the Commandant Yan Mi proposed Danyang lake-field works—building Puli Pool.

value.zh: 詔百官會議，咸以為用功多而田不保成，唯興以為可成。
value.en: Ministers called the dyke a boondoggle—Puyang Xing alone swore it would pay.
value.literal: Edict ordered hundred offices conference—all judged labor vast while fields might not hold—only Xing deemed it doable.

value.zh: 遂會諸兵民就作，功傭之費不可勝數，士卒死亡，或自賊殺，百姓大怨之。
value.en: Corvée swelled—paymasters drowned—troops died in mutiny and accident—the delta cursed Xing’s name.
value.literal: Thereupon assembled troops and civilians to labor—merit-pay costs beyond counting—soldiers died—some killed each other—commoners bitterly resented.

value.zh: 興遷為丞相，與休寵臣左將軍張共布相表裡，邦內失望。
value.en: Raised to chancellor, he teamed with Zhang Bu—Wu groaned at crony rule.
value.literal: Xing promoted Chancellor—joined Xiu’s favored minister General of the Left Zhang Bu (the transmitted text inserts a stray graph between the two syllables of the name)—mutual inside-out—the state inwardly despaired.

value.zh: 七年七月，休薨。
value.en: Sun Xiu died in the seventh month of the seventh year of his era.
value.literal: Seventh month seventh year Xiu died.

value.zh: 左典軍萬彧素與烏程侯孫皓善，乃勸興、布，於是興、布廢休適子而迎立皓。
value.en: Wan Yu talked Xing and Bu into skipping Xiu’s son for Sun Hao.
value.literal: Left Army Clerk Wan Yu long favored Marquis of Wucheng Sun Hao—thereupon urged Xing and Bu—thus Xing and Bu deposed Xiu’s heir son of proper line and welcomed Hao.

value.zh: 皓既踐阼，加興侍中，領青州牧。
value.en: Sun Hao bought loyalty with palace posts and a Qingzhou title.
value.literal: Once Hao mounted throne he added Xing Palace Attendant concurrent Governor of Qingzhou.

value.zh: 俄彧譖興、布追悔前事。
value.en: Wan Yu then whispered that both ministers regretted enthroning him.
value.literal: Soon Yu slandered Xing and Bu—regretting prior deeds.

value.zh: 十一月朔入朝，皓因收興、布，徙廣州，道追殺之，夷三族。
value.en: On the new moon Hao arrested them—marched them toward Guangzhou—had them killed en route—then wiped three degrees of kin.
value.literal: First day eleventh month court entry—Hao thereupon seized Xing and Bu—banished Guangzhou—agents overtook them on road killing—extinguished three clans.

value.zh: 綝遣將軍孫耽送亮之國，徙尚於零陵，遷公主於豫章。
value.en: Sun Lin sent Sun Dan to escort Sun Liang to his fief, banished Quan Shang to Lingling, and moved the princess to Yuzhang.
value.literal: Lin sent General Sun Dan to escort Liang to his fief, moved Shang to Lingling, and transferred the princess to Yuzhang.

value.zh: 綝意彌溢，侮慢民神，遂燒大橋頭伍子胥廟，又壞浮屠祠，斬道人。
value.en: Sun Lin grew ever more arrogant, insulted gods and people, burned the Wu Zixu temple at Daqiao, wrecked Buddhist shrines, and executed Daoist clergy.
value.literal: Lin's arrogance overflowed; he insulted folk spirits, burned the Wu Zixu temple at Daqiao, destroyed Buddhist shrines, and executed Daoist clergy.

value.zh: 休既即位，稱草莽臣。
value.en: Once Emperor Xiu reigned, Sun Lin called himself a rustic subject.
value.literal: After Xiu took the throne, Lin styled himself a rustic subject.

value.zh: 詣闕上書曰：「臣伏自省，才非干國，因緣肺腑，位極人臣，傷錦敗駕，罪負彰露，尋愆惟闕，夙夜憂懼。
value.en: He went to court and wrote, "I reflect that my talent cannot sustain the state, yet kinship raised me to the summit of power; I have torn brocade and wrecked the carriage, and guilt stands clear; day and night I fear my faults.
value.literal: He went to court and submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject reflects in humility: talent unfit to sustain the state, yet through kinship rose to the summit of ministers; I have torn brocade and wrecked the carriage—guilt stands revealed; reviewing faults I fear day and night.

value.zh: 臣聞天命棐諶，必就有德，是以幽、厲失度，閡宣中興，陛下聖德，纂承大統，宜得良輔；
value.en: Heaven aids the sincere and settles on virtue; You and Li lost the way yet Xuan restored the house; Your Majesty inherits the great succession and deserves worthy assistants;
value.literal: Your subject has heard that Heaven's mandate is aided and sincere and must settle on the virtuous; thus You and Li lost measure yet Xuan restored the house; Your Majesty's sagely virtue inherits the great succession and deserves worthy assistants;

value.zh: 以協雍熙，雖堯之盛，猶求稷契之佐；
value.en: to harmonize peace; even Yao sought men like Ji and Qi;
value.literal: to harmonize peace and glory; even in Yao's greatness he still sought assistants like Ji and Qi;

value.zh: 以協明聖之德。
value.en: to match enlightened and sagely virtue.
value.literal: to harmonize with enlightened and sagely virtue.

value.zh: 古人有言：『陳力就列，不能者止。』
value.en: The ancients said, "Offer strength and take your place; if unable, withdraw."
value.literal: The ancients said, "Offer strength and take your place; if unable, withdraw."

value.zh: 臣雖自展竭，無益庶政，謹上印綬節鉞，退還田裡，以避賢路。」
value.en: Though I have exhausted myself I benefit no governance; I return seals, ribbons, and the staff of authority, withdraw to my fields, and yield the path for the worthy."
value.literal: Though your subject has exhausted himself, he benefits no common governance; I respectfully return seals, ribbons, and credential staff, withdraw to fields and hamlets, and yield the path for the worthy."

value.zh: 休引見慰喻。
value.en: Emperor Xiu received him in audience and comforted him.
value.literal: Xiu received him in audience and comforted him.

value.zh: 又下詔曰：「朕以不德，守藩於外，值茲際會，群公卿士，暨於朕躬，以奉宗廟。
value.en: He also issued an edict: "Lacking virtue I guarded a fief abroad until this juncture, when lords and ministers with me uphold the ancestral temple.
value.literal: He also issued an edict saying, "We lack virtue, guarded a fief abroad, met this juncture, and lords, ministers, and scholars together with Our person uphold the ancestral temple.

value.zh: 朕用撫然，若涉淵冰。
value.en: I am apprehensive, as if treading deep ice.
value.literal: We are apprehensive, as if treading deep ice.

value.zh: 大將軍忠計內發，扶危定傾，安康社稷，功勳赫然。
value.en: The grand general's loyal counsel braced peril, steadied the state, and his merit blazed bright.
value.literal: The Grand General's loyal plan arose within, braced peril and steadied the tipping, brought peace to altars and state, and his merit blazed bright.

value.zh: 昔漢孝宣踐阼，霍光尊顯，褒德賞功，古今之通義也。
value.en: When Emperor Xuan of Han took the throne he honored Huo Guang—praising merit is the constant way of past and present.
value.literal: Formerly when Han's Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, Huo Guang was honored and exalted—praising virtue and rewarding merit is the constant principle of past and present.

value.zh: 其以大將軍為丞相、荊州牧，食五縣。」
value.en: Let the grand general be chancellor and governor of Jing with income from five counties."
value.literal: Let the Grand General be Chancellor and Governor of Jing Province with income from five counties."

value.zh: 恩為禦史大夫、衛將軍，據右將軍。
value.en: En was made grandee secretary and guard general; Lü Ju was made general of the right.
value.literal: En was made Grandee Secretary and Guard General; Ju was made General of the Right.

value.zh: 皆縣侯。
value.en: All were enfeoffed as district marquises.
value.literal: All were enfeoffed as district marquises.

value.zh: 幹雜號將軍、亭侯。
value.en: Gan was made a miscellaneous-number general and village marquis.
value.literal: Gan was made a miscellaneous-number general and village marquis.

value.zh: 闓亦封亭侯。
value.en: Kan was also enfeoffed as village marquis.
value.literal: Kan was also enfeoffed as village marquis.

value.zh: 綝一門五侯，皆典禁兵，權傾人主，自吳國朝臣未嘗有也。
value.en: Five marquises in one Sun Lin household, all commanding palace troops—power beyond any Wu minister before.
value.literal: Lin's household held five marquisates at once, all commanding forbidden troops; power tilted past the sovereign—never before among Wu court ministers.

value.zh: 永安元年258年十二月丁卯，建業中謠言明會有變。
value.en: Yongan 1, month 12, day dingmao (258): Jianye rumor warned of trouble at the bright assembly.
value.literal: In the twelfth month, day dingmao, of the first year of Yongan, 258 CE, Jianye rumor said the bright assembly would bring upheaval.

value.zh: 綝聞之，不悅。
value.en: Sun Lin heard and was displeased.
value.literal: Lin heard it and was displeased.

value.zh: 夜大風發木揚沙，綝益恐。
value.en: That night gale winds uprooted trees and raised sand; Lin grew more afraid.
value.literal: That night a great wind uprooted trees and raised sand; Lin grew more fearful.

value.zh: 戊辰臘會，綝稱疾。
value.en: At the year-end assembly on day wuchen Sun Lin claimed illness.
value.literal: On day wuchen at the year-end assembly Lin claimed illness.

value.zh: 休強起之，使者十餘輩。
value.en: Emperor Xiu forced him to attend; more than ten messengers came.
value.literal: Xiu forced him to rise; over ten messengers came.

value.zh: 綝不得已，將人，眾止焉。
value.en: Sun Lin had no choice and was about to bring men when the crowd stopped him.
value.literal: Lin had no choice and was about to lead men when the crowd stopped him.

value.zh: 綝曰：「國家屢有命，不可辭。
value.en: Sun Lin said, "The state has repeatedly commanded; I cannot refuse.
value.literal: Lin said, "The state has repeatedly commanded; one cannot refuse.

value.zh: 可豫整兵，令府內起火，因是可得速還。」
value.en: Ready troops in advance, set fire inside the mansion, and I can return quickly."
value.literal: You may ready troops in advance, set fire inside the mansion, and thereby return quickly."

value.zh: 遂入，尋而火起，綝求出，休曰：「外兵自多，不足煩丞相也。」
value.en: He entered; soon fire rose; Lin begged to leave; Emperor Xiu said, "Outside troops are plentiful—no need to trouble the chancellor."
value.literal: He then entered; soon fire rose; Lin begged to leave; Xiu said, "Outside troops are plentiful enough—no need to trouble the Chancellor."

value.zh: 綝起離席，奉、布目左右縛之。
value.en: Sun Lin rose; Ding Feng and Zhang Bu signaled attendants to bind him.
value.literal: Lin rose from his seat; Feng and Bu signaled attendants to bind him.

value.zh: 綝叩首曰：「願徙交州。」
value.en: Lin kowtowed: "Banish me to Jiaozhou."
value.literal: Lin kowtowed and said, "I wish to be banished to Jiaozhou."

value.zh: 休曰：「卿何以不徙滕胤、呂據？」
value.en: Emperor Xiu said, "Why did you not banish Teng Yin and Lü Ju?"
value.literal: Xiu said, "Why did you not banish Teng Yin and Lü Ju?"

value.zh: 綝復曰：「願沒為官奴。」
value.en: Lin said, "Make me a government slave."
value.literal: Lin again said, "I wish to be reduced to government slaves."

value.zh: 休曰：「何不以胤、據為奴乎！」
value.en: Emperor Xiu said, "Why not make Yin and Ju the slaves!"
value.literal: Xiu said, "Why not make Yin and Ju the slaves!"

value.zh: 遂斬之。
value.en: Then he was beheaded.
value.literal: Thereupon he was beheaded.

value.zh: 以綝首令其眾曰：「諸與綝同謀皆赦。」
value.en: Holding Lin's head he told the host, "All who plotted with Lin are pardoned."
value.literal: With Lin's head he addressed the host saying, "All who plotted with Lin are pardoned."

value.zh: 放仗者五千人。
value.en: Five thousand who laid down weapons were released.
value.literal: Five thousand who laid down weapons were released.

value.zh: 闓乘船欲北降，追殺之。
value.en: Kan tried to flee north by ship; pursuers killed him.
value.literal: Kan took ship intending to surrender north; pursuers killed him.

value.zh: 夷三族。
value.en: Three clans were exterminated.
value.literal: Three clans were exterminated.

value.zh: 發孫峻棺，取其印綬，綝其木而埋之，以殺魯育等故也。
value.en: Sun Jun's coffin was opened, his seals taken, the wood flayed and buried—for the killing of Lu Yu and others.
value.literal: Sun Jun's coffin was opened, his seals and ribbons taken, the wood flayed and buried—because of the killing of Lu Yu and others.

value.zh: 濮陽興字子元，陳留人也。
value.en: Puyang Xing, styled Ziyuan, came from Chenliu.
value.literal: Puyang Xing, courtesy name Ziyuan, was a man of Chenliu.

value.zh: 父逸，漢末避亂江東，官至長沙太守。
value.en: His father Yi fled the late-Han turmoil to Jiangdong and became administrator of Changsha.
value.literal: His father Yi, fleeing chaos at the end of Han, crossed to Jiangdong and rose to Administrator of Changsha.

value.zh: 逸事見《陸瑁傳》。
value.en: Yi's career is recorded in the biography of Lu Mao.
value.literal: Yi's career appears in the biography of Lu Mao.

value.zh: 興少有士名，孫權時除上虞令，稍遷至尚書左曹，以五官中郎將使蜀，還為會稽太守。
value.en: Puyang Xing won early fame as a gentleman; under Sun Quan he served as magistrate of Shangyu, rose through the secretariat, went to Shu as envoy, and returned as administrator of Kuaiji.
value.literal: Xing early gained a scholar's reputation; under Sun Quan he was appointed magistrate of Shangyu, gradually rose to the left bureau of the Masters of Writing, served as General of the Five Offices as envoy to Shu, and on return became Administrator of Kuaiji.

value.zh: 時琅邪王休居會稽，興深與相結。
value.en: While Prince Xiu of Langye lived in Kuaiji, Puyang Xing became his close ally.
value.literal: At that time Prince of Langye Xiu resided in Kuaiji, and Xing formed a deep bond with him.

value.zh: 及休即位，徵興為太常衛將軍、平軍國事，封外黃侯。
value.en: When Emperor Xiu ascended the throne, Xing was made chamberlain for ceremonies and guard general, charged with military affairs, and enfeoffed as marquis of Waihuang.
value.literal: When Xiu took the throne, Xing was summoned as Chamberlain for Ceremonies and Guard General and charged with settling military affairs, enfeoffed as Marquis of Waihuang.

value.zh: 永安三年260年，都尉嚴密建丹楊湖田，作浦裡塘。
value.en: Yongan 3 (260): Commandant Yan Mi proposed the Danyang lake-field project and the Puli reclamation.
value.literal: In the third year of Yongan, 260 CE, Commandant Yan Mi proposed Danyang lake-field works, building Puli Pool.

value.zh: 王蕃字永元，廬江人也。
value.en: Wang Fan, courtesy name Yongyuan, came from Lujiang commandery.
value.literal: Wang Fan, courtesy name Yongyuan, was a man of Lujiang.

value.zh: 博覽多聞，兼通術藝。
value.en: He was widely read and well informed, and equally at home with astronomy, mathematics, and the technical arts.
value.literal: He read widely and heard much, and was also versed in technical arts.

value.zh: 始為尚書郎，去官。
value.en: He began as a gentleman clerk in the secretariat, then resigned his post.
value.literal: At first he was gentleman of the masters of writing, then left office.

value.zh: 孫休即位，與賀邵、薛瑩、虞汜俱為散騎中常侍，皆加駙馬都尉。
value.en: When Sun Xiu took the throne, Wang Fan, He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si were all named attendants at ease and regular palace attendants, each with the additional title chief commandant of carriage escort.
value.literal: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, together with He Shao, Xue Ying, and Yu Si he became attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and to each was added chief commandant of carriage escort.

value.zh: 時論清之。
value.en: Public opinion ranked them among the court's clearest spirits.
value.literal: Contemporary opinion deemed them pure.

value.zh: 遣使至蜀，蜀人稱焉，還為夏口監軍。
value.en: Sent on embassy to Shu, he won high praise there; on his return he was named supervisor of the army at Xiakou.
value.literal: He was sent as envoy to Shu; the people of Shu praised him, and on return he became supervisor of the army at Xiakou.

value.zh: 丞相陸凱上疏曰："常侍王蕃黃中通理，知天知物，處朝忠蹇，斯社稷之重鎮，大吳之龍逢也。
value.en: Lu Kai memorialized: Wang Fan is the inner integrity and clear judgment of the court—Wu's pillar, your Long Pang.
value.literal: Chancellor Lu Kai submitted a memorial saying: Regular attendant Wang Fan is yellow within and comprehends principle; he knows Heaven and knows things; in court he is loyal and outspoken—he is the heavy bulwark of the altars of soil and grain, the Long Pang of great Wu.

value.zh: 昔事景皇，納言左右，景皇欽嘉，歎為異倫。
value.en: He served Emperor Jing as a candid advisor and won that emperor's open admiration.
value.literal: In former times he served Emperor Jing, speaking out at the ruler's side; Emperor Jing admired and praised him, sighing that he was of a different class.

value.zh: 而陛下忿其苦辭，惡其直對，梟之殿堂，屍骸暴棄，邦內傷心，有識悲悼。
value.en: Yet you resented his blunt speech, executed him in open court, and left his body unburied—the whole court grieves, every thoughtful man mourns.
value.literal: Yet Your Majesty resented his bitter words, hated his straight replies, displayed him in the hall, and his corpse was cast aside exposed—within the state hearts are wounded, those with understanding mourn in grief.

value.zh: "其痛蕃如此。
value.en: Such was Lu Kai's grief for Wang Fan.
value.literal: Thus he grieved for Fan to this degree.

value.zh: 蕃死時年三十九，皓徙蕃家屬廣州。
value.en: Wang Fan died at thirty-nine; Sun Hao banished his kin to Guangzhou.
value.literal: When Fan died he was thirty-nine years old; Hao moved Fan's family dependants to Guangzhou.

value.zh: 二弟著、延皆作佳器，郭馬起事，不為馬用，見害。
value.en: His brothers Wang Zhu and Wang Yan were both promising men; when Guo Ma rose in revolt they refused to serve him and were put to death.
value.literal: His two younger brothers Zhu and Yan were both fine vessels; when Guo Ma raised an affair, they would not serve Ma and were killed.

value.zh: 樓玄字承先，沛郡蘄人也。
value.en: Lou Xuan, courtesy name Chengxian, came from Qi in Pei commandery.
value.literal: Lou Xuan, courtesy name Chengxian, was a man of Qi in Pei commandery.

value.zh: 孫休時為監農御史。
value.en: Under Sun Xiu he served as censor of agriculture.
value.literal: In Sun Xiu's time he was censor who supervises agriculture.

value.zh: 孫皓即位，與王蕃、郭逴、萬彧俱為散騎中常侍，出為會稽太守，入為大司農。
value.en: When Sun Hao took the throne, Lou Xuan joined Wang Fan, Guo Chuo, and Wan Yu as attendants at ease and regular palace attendants, then served as grand administrator of Kuaiji and grand minister of agriculture.
value.literal: When Sun Hao ascended the throne, together with Wang Fan, Guo Chuo, and Wan Yu he became all attendant at ease and regular palace attendant; he went out as grand administrator of Kuaiji and entered as grand minister of agriculture.

value.zh: 舊禁中主者自用親近人作之，彧陳親密近職宜用好人，皓因敕有司，求忠清之士，以應其選，遂用玄為宮下鎮禁中候，主殿中事，玄從九卿持刀侍衛，正身率眾，奉法而行，應對切直，數迕皓意，漸見責怒。
value.en: By old practice, posts inside the forbidden precinct had always gone to favorites. Wan Yu argued that intimate inner offices should employ good men, so Sun Hao ordered the offices to seek loyal and incorrupt gentlemen and chose Lou Xuan as Colonel Garrisoning the Forbidden Interior below the palace, in charge of affairs within the halls. Ranking with the nine ministers, Lou Xuan carried the blade as an imperial guard, corrected himself and led the others, acted according to law, and answered sharply and directly. He repeatedly crossed Hao’s wishes and gradually drew blame and anger.
value.literal: By old practice those in charge within the forbidden precincts always used intimate men for the post; Yu presented that intimate near offices ought to employ good men; Hao thereupon ordered the responsible offices to seek loyal and pure gentlemen to meet that selection, and so used Xuan as palace-base colonel who garrisons the forbidden interior, in charge of hall affairs—Xuan, ranking with the nine ministers, bore the blade as bodyguard, corrected his person and led the host, acted by the law, answered cuttingly and straight, repeatedly went against Hao's intent, and gradually met blame and anger.

value.zh: 後人誣白玄與賀邵相逢，駐共耳語大笑，謗訕政事，遂被詔詰責，送付廣州。
value.en: Later a informer claimed he had stopped in the road with He Shao, whispered and laughed, and mocked policy; an edict condemned him and he was banished to Guangzhou.
value.literal: Afterward someone falsely reported that Xuan, meeting He Shao, halted and together whispered in the ear and laughed greatly, slandering and mocking government affairs; thereupon he received an edict of interrogation and blame and was sent off to Guangzhou.

value.zh: 賀邵字興伯，會稽山陰人也，
value.en: He Shao, courtesy name Xingbo, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji
value.literal: He Shao, courtesy name Xingbo, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji,

value.zh: 〈吴书曰：邵，贺齐之孙，景之子。〉
value.en: 〈The Book of Wu identifies him as He Qi's grandson and He Jing's son.〉
value.literal: 〈The Book of Wu states: Shao was grandson of He Qi, son of Jing.〉

value.zh: 孫休即位，從中郎為散騎中常侍，出為吳郡太守。
value.en: When Sun Xiu took the throne he rose from gentleman of the palace to attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, then became grand administrator of Wu.
value.literal: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, he went from gentleman of the palace to attendant at ease and regular palace attendant, and went out as grand administrator of Wu commandery.

value.zh: 孫皓時，入為左典軍，遷中書令，領太子太傅。
value.en: Under Sun Hao he became left army supervisor, then director of the secretariat, while serving as grand tutor to the heir apparent.
value.literal: In Sun Hao's time he entered as left army supervisor, was transferred to director of the secretariat, and concurrently held grand tutor to the heir apparent.

value.zh: 臣聞興國之君樂聞其過，荒亂之主樂聞其譽。
value.en: A rising king loves to hear his faults; a doomed king loves praise.
value.literal: Your servant has heard that the lord who raises a state delights to hear his faults, while the lord of wasteland and chaos delights to hear his praise.

value.zh: 聞其過者過日消而福臻，聞其譽者譽日損而禍至。
value.en: Faults heard shrink and fortune grows; praise heard swells and calamity nears.
value.literal: He who hears his faults—faults daily diminish and blessing arrives; he who hears his praise—praise daily shrinks and disaster comes.

value.zh: 是以古之人君，捐讓以進賢，虛己以求過，譬天位於乘□，以虎尾為警戒。
value.en: The ancients yielded to bring forward talent and took the throne as riding rotten wood beside a tiger's tail.
value.literal: Therefore the lords of old yielded place to advance the worthy, emptied themselves to seek faults, likened the heavenly seat to riding a rotten log, and took the tiger's tail as warning.

value.zh: 至於陛下，嚴刑法以禁直辭，黜善士以逆諫臣，眩耀毀譽之實，沉淪近習之言。
value.en: You silence candor with cruel law, exile good men who remonstrate, chase gossip, and drown in favorites' whispers.
value.literal: As for Your Majesty, you use harsh punishments to forbid straight speech, dismiss good gentlemen to reject remonstrating ministers, dazzle yourself with the reality of slander and praise, and sink in the words of those near at hand.

value.zh: 昔高宗思佐，夢寐得賢，而陛下求之如忘，忽之如遺。
value.en: Gaozong dreamed his ministers; you forget yours and toss them aside.
value.literal: In olden times Gaozong thought on helpers and in dream and sleep obtained the worthy; Your Majesty seeks them as if forgotten, neglects them as if cast away.

value.zh: 故常侍王蕃忠恪在公，才任輔弼，以醉酒之間加之大戮。
value.en: Wang Fan was fit to be your pillar—you slew him for a drunken slip.
value.literal: Therefore regular attendant Wang Fan was loyal and careful in public service, his talent fit to assist and guide—over drunkenness in a feast you added the great execution.

value.zh: 近鴻臚葛奚，先帝舊臣，偶有逆迕，昏醉之言耳，三爵之後，禮所不諱，陛下猥發雷霆，謂之輕慢，飲之醇酒，中毒隕命。
value.en: Ge Xi, an elder statesman, misspoke while drunk—rites forgive what follows three cups—yet you called it lese-majesty, forced strong wine on him, and he died of poison.
value.literal: Recently grand herald Ge Xi, an old minister of the late emperor, once by chance was contrary and disobedient—it was words of muddled drunkenness; after three goblets, what rites do not excuse—Your Majesty rashly loosed thunder, calling it slighting and irreverent, made him drink strong wine, and he was poisoned and lost his life.

value.zh: 自是之後，海內悼心，朝臣失圖，仕者以退為幸，居者以出為福，誠非所以保光洪緒，臣隆道化也。
value.en: Officials now count leaving office as luck and staying home as blessing—no way to preserve the dynasty or spread moral rule.
value.literal: From this time within the seas mourn in heart, court ministers lose their bearings; those in office take retirement as fortune, those at home take going out as blessing—this is truly not the means to preserve the bright great line and extend the transforming Way.

value.zh: 和廢後，為黃門侍郎。
value.en: After Prince He's deposition Wei Yao became gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.
value.literal: After He was deposed, he became gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.

value.zh: 孫亮即位，諸葛恪輔政，表曜為太史令，撰《吳書》，華核、薛瑩等皆與參同，孫休踐阼，為中書郎、博士祭酒。
value.en: When Sun Liang took the throne, Zhuge Ke as regent recommended Yao as grand astrologer to compile the Book of Wu; Hua He, Xue Ying, and others all took part. When Sun Xiu acceded, Yao became gentleman of the secretariat and libationer of the erudits.
value.literal: When Sun Liang ascended the throne, Zhuge Ke governed and memorialized Yao as grand astrologer to compose the Book of Wu; Hua He, Xue Ying, and others all joined in the same work; when Sun Xiu mounted the steps, he was gentleman of the secretariat and libationer of erudits.

value.zh: 命曜依劉向故事，校定眾書。
value.en: Sun Xiu ordered him to collate the imperial library on Liu Xiang's model.
value.literal: He ordered Yao according to Liu Xiang's precedent to collate and fix the multitude of books.

value.zh: 又欲延曜侍講，而左將軍張布近習寵幸，事行多玷，憚曜侍講儒士，又性精確，懼以古今警戒休意，固爭不可。
value.en: He wished Wei Yao to lecture the throne, but Zhang Bu, the favorite general, blocked it, fearing a scholar would lecture Sun Xiu on moral history.
value.literal: He also wished to extend Yao as lecturer-in-waiting, but General of the Left Zhang Bu was a near attendant, favored and doted on, his deeds many times stained; he feared Yao as lecturer, a Confucian gentleman, and moreover by nature precise, feared he would use past and present to warn Xiu's intent—therefore he firmly contended that it could not be done.

value.zh: 休深恨布，語在《休傳》。
value.en: Sun Xiu came to hate Zhang Bu—the story is told in Sun Xiu's biography.
value.literal: Xiu deeply hated Bu—the words are in the biography of Xiu.

value.zh: 然曜竟止不入。
value.en: Wei Yao never took the lecturer's post.
value.literal: Yet in the end Yao stopped and did not enter.

value.zh: 志第十三 天文一
value.en: Treatise Thirteen: Astronomy, Part One
value.literal: Treatise 13: Astronomy 1

value.zh: 魏高貴鄉公正元元年十一月，有白氣出斗側，廣數丈，長竟天。
value.en: Under Wei emperor Cao Mao, Zhengyuan 1, eleventh month: white vapor rose beside the Dipper, several fathoms wide, streaking the length of the sky.
value.literal: Wei, Duke of Gaoguixiang, Zhengyuan year 1, eleventh month: white vapor emerged from the side of Dipper, several zhang wide, stretching the length of the sky.

value.zh: 王肅曰：「蚩尤之旗也，東南其有亂乎！」
value.en: Wang Su said: "That is Chiyou's banner—surely the southeast will erupt in rebellion!"
value.literal: Wang Su said: "This is the banner of Chiyou—is there rebellion in the southeast?"

value.zh: 二年正月，毋丘儉等據淮南以叛，大將軍司馬師討平之。
value.en: Zhengyuan 2, first month: Guanqiu Jian seized Huainan in revolt; Grand General Sima Shi crushed the rebellion.
value.literal: Year 2, first month, Guanqiu Jian and others held Huainan in rebellion; Grand General Sima Shi suppressed and pacified them.

value.zh: 案占，「蚩尤旗見，王者征伐四方。」
value.en: Per the prognostications: "When Chiyou's banner appears, the sovereign marches to war on every front."
value.literal: Per astrological texts: "When Chiyou's banner appears, the king campaigns in all four directions."

value.zh: 自後又征淮南，西平巴蜀。
value.en: Thereafter the court campaigned again in Huainan and pacified Ba and Shu in the west.
value.literal: Afterwards there were again campaigns against Huainan and the pacification of Ba-Shu in the west.

value.zh: 是歲，吳主孫亮五鳳元年，斗牛，吳、越分。
value.en: That same year Sun Liang of Wu entered his Wufeng reign: the Dipper and Ox govern Wu and Yue's domain.
value.literal: That year, Wu ruler Sun Liang's Wufeng year 1: Dipper-Ox—Wu and Yue's allotted field.

value.zh: 案占：「有兵喪，除舊佈新之象也。」
value.en: Per the prognostications: "War and mourning follow—the omen of sweeping away the old and installing the new."
value.literal: Checking the prognostications: "There is warfare and mourning—the sign of removing the old and spreading the new."

value.zh: 太平三年，孫綝盛兵圍宮，廢亮為會稽王，孫休代立，是其應也。
value.en: In Taiping 3, Sun Chen marched on the palace, deposed Sun Liang as King of Kuaiji, and installed Sun Xiu in his place—the omen fulfilled.
value.literal: Taiping year 3, Sun Chen massed troops and besieged the palace, deposed Liang as King of Kuaiji, and Sun Xiu succeeded him—this was its fulfillment.

value.zh: 故國志又書于吳。
value.en: Hence the Records of the Three Kingdoms places the entry under Wu as well.
value.literal: Therefore the Records of the Three Kingdoms also records it under Wu.

value.zh: 由是淮南江東同揚州地，故于時變見吳、楚之分。
value.en: Because Huainan and Jiangdong both lay within Yang Province, the portents of that era clustered in the Wu and Chu domains.
value.literal: From this, Huainan and Jiangdong share Yang Province territory, so celestial anomalies of the time appeared in Wu and Chu's allotted fields.

value.zh: 則魏之淮南，多與吳同災，是以毋丘儉以孛為己應，遂起兵而敗，又其應也。
value.en: Wei's Huainan and Wu often suffered the same omens; Guanqiu Jian read the comet as his personal sign, rose in revolt, and was crushed—yet another fulfillment.
value.literal: Thus Wei's Huainan often shared calamities with Wu; Guanqiu Jian took the broom star as his own omen, raised troops and was defeated—again its fulfillment.

value.zh: 後三年，即魏甘露二年，諸葛誕又反淮南，吳遣硃異救之。
value.en: Three years on—in Wei Ganlu 2—Zhuge Dan rebelled again in Huainan, and Wu dispatched Zhu Yi to his aid.
value.literal: Three years later, Wei Ganlu year 2, Zhuge Dan again rebelled in Huainan; Wu sent Zhu Yi to rescue him.

value.zh: 及城陷，誕眾吳兵死沒各數萬人，猶前長星之應也。
value.en: When the city fell, tens of thousands on both sides—Dan's men and Wu's relief force—were killed, fulfilling the earlier comet's warning.
value.literal: When the city fell, tens of thousands each among Dan's followers and Wu's soldiers died and perished—still the fulfillment of the earlier long star.

value.zh: 高貴鄉公正元二年二月戊午，熒惑犯東井北轅西頭第一星。
value.en: Under Cao Mao, Zhengyuan 2, second month, day wuwu: Mars crossed the westernmost star at the northern yoke of Eastern Well.
